standard_prerequisites.name: Archimedean property of the Cauchy reals
standard_prerequisites.statement: Every real is bounded in absolute value by some natural number.
standard_prerequisites.use: It makes the map from Sigma n, [-n,n] to RC surjective at source lines 1649-1658.

standard_prerequisites.name: Extension of Lipschitz maps
standard_prerequisites.statement: A Lipschitz map on the rationals extends to a Lipschitz map on the reals with the same constant.
standard_prerequisites.use: It is applied to the squaring map on each bounded interval at source lines 1666-1668.

standard_prerequisites.name: Uniqueness of factorisation through a surjection
standard_prerequisites.statement: A map respecting the kernel pair of a surjection factors uniquely through it.
standard_prerequisites.use: It produces the unique function at source lines 1671-1679.

core_obligations: Use the archimedean property to show that e : (Sigma n:N, [-n,n]) -> RC is surjective (source lines 1649-1658).

For each n, observe that squaring on the bounded rational interval is Lipschitz with constant 2n, and extend it to sbar_n : [-n,n] -> RC with the same constant using the retained extension result, with the interval details left to the cited exercise (source lines 1658-1668).

Show that the maps sbar_n are compatible on overlaps: for m < n the restrictions agree because both are Lipschitz and hence continuous in the sense of the retained continuity result (source lines 1668-1671).
Apply the retained factorisation result for surjections to the map (n,x) |-> s_n(x) to obtain the unique function on RC (source lines 1671-1679).

proof_roadmap.step: Surjectivity of the bounded-interval cover from the archimedean property.
Extend squaring on each bounded interval by the retained Lipschitz extension.
Compatibility of the extensions via continuity.

difficulty_reason: Counted unit is Theorem 11.3.46 at source lines 1636-1646: squaring of rationals extends to a unique function on the Cauchy reals with the explicit Lipschitz bound |u^2 - v^2| <= 2 n |u - v| on [-n,n]. The author's proof (source lines 1648-1680) assembles four separate inputs rather than computing directly: the archimedean property makes the bounded-interval cover surjective onto RC (lines 1649-1658), the retained extension theorem turns squaring on each bounded rational interval, which is Lipschitz with constant 2n, into a map on that interval (lines 1658-1668), compatibility of these extensions on overlaps is deduced from continuity via the retained continuity lemma (lines 1668-1671), and uniqueness is obtained by factoring through the surjection using the retained factorisation result (lines 1671-1679). The statement is a single existence-and-uniqueness assertion with an estimate, and records none of the four steps.
